messages:
kevin: Heads-up — ran the ad-hoc access certification after the vuln triage.
kevin: Found ~18 principals with admin-level bindings to KMS keys that shouldn't be elevated.
kevin: Repro query I ran:
kevin: ```
kevin: SELECT principal, role, resource FROM iam_bindings WHERE resource LIKE '%kms%' AND role LIKE '%admin%';
kevin: ```
sara: :eyes: can you paste the top 5? we should check ownerless service accounts first.
kevin: Pasted in thread — top ones are svc-ml-ingest, infra-deploy-bot, legacy-ci, analytics-worker, monitoring-bridge.
mike: legacy-ci and analytics-worker are on the long-lived list. analytics-worker was supposed to be scoped to encrypt-decrypt only.
jon: I remember a note from the Dedicated oncall about analytics-worker doing key import for historic data. might explain the admin binding.
hannah: audit-bot flagged a spike in KMS key creation and imports last week (see run id 2026-03-12_07). link: https://internal.redwood/run/2026-03-12_07
audit-bot: Automated finding: 18 admin KMS bindings, 6 principals unassociated with current owner groups. Severity: medium-high. Suggested remediation: owners must justify via evidence link or binding will be revoked in 72h.
kevin: Proposal: do a 48h owners notification -> 72h automatic prune if no evidence. we should exempt oncall/service accounts with current incident tags.
sara: Agree. Also request a short playbook for exemptions. we need a safe rollback path if revoke breaks deploys.
mike: Quick rollback pattern: reapply binding and trigger canary deploy to the single affected env, then escalate. I'll draft the CLI commands.
mike: CLI snippet:
mike: ```
mike: redwood-iam revoke --principal svc-analytics-worker --role kms.admin --dry-run
mike: redwood-iam grant --principal svc-analytics-worker --role kms.encrypt_decrypt --resource projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*
mike: ```
jon: Could we automate evidence collection? owners could drop a ticket id or short justification in the notification thread.
hannah: I'll add an optional structured form in the notif with fields: owner-team, ticket-id, expiry-date, reason. that'll make auditing easier.
kevin: Action items:
kevin: 1) hannah to extend notif with structured form (ETA 24h)
kevin: 2) mike to prepare dry-run and rollback commands + validation checklist (ETA 24h)
kevin: 3) sara to compile owner list and reach out to biz-owners (ETA 48h)
kevin: 4) jon to add temporary canary policy and exemption label for oncall (ETA 12h)
sara: I'll also cross-check with the private deployment customers list — we may need to coordinate for Private KMS keys.
jon: For the automation, can we tag keys with `managed_by=redwood-iam` so future scans are easier?
kevin: yes — add that to the remediation checklist.
mike: one more thing — make sure we log revokes with correlation id to KMS audit log so we can revert cleanly if needed.
hannah: Noted. I'll include sample audit-log query templates in the playbook.
kevin: If anyone sees a live incident after we revoke, ping #eng-oncall and I’ll block further revokes.
sara: :thumbsup: will coordinate owners outreach now.
kevin: thanks all — I'll open the PR for the prune job once mike's dry-run is ready. tagging @audit-bot for tracking.
audit-bot: Tracking ticket created: A-2026-8893. Current status: pending owners input.
jon: will drop a short blurb in #all-hands about the certification cadence once we have dates. :spiral_calendar:
kevin: PR link (draft): https://git.internal/redwood/security/prs/4021 — includes alert templates and the revoke job.
mike: I'll run the dry-run in staging tomorrow morning and post results here.
hannah: ETA for playbook update: EOD tomorrow.
kevin: Great. closing loop here — we'll meet after the dry-run to agree on timing for prune. :checkered_flag:
